correctness.rationale: PASS for the replacement. The frozen metadata and proof intend i.i.d. regeneration, but the listed hypotheses say only a common failed-cycle law and independence of the next exploration, which do not themselves justify the geometric product of failed-cycle transforms. The replacement explicitly makes each fixed-law Brownian exploration and clock independent of the complete history preceding it, and proves the claim without i.i.d. returns. On the event of m failures and completed returns the elapsed time S_m and all prefix information are known. Testing the final success against that prefix gives the joint side-time transform as f_j(s) times the sum over m of E[exp(-s S_m); N>m]. Success has constant probability p, so N is geometric and the sum is finite, but its individual nonzero-s summands need not be powers. Testing arbitrary bounded functions gives independence of stopped prefix and successful exploration; the common factor cancels between normalized sides. The killed Dirichlet weights are proportional to sinh(b sqrt((r+s)/D)) and sinh(a sqrt((r+s)/D)); the ratio is the Laplace transform of the independent interval-(0,b) hitting time at b from a, conditioned to hit b first and exponentially tilted at r. This gives the convolution by uniqueness. The individual sinh-product factors are Bernoulli–exponential transforms with a summable expectation and positive variance; the Lévy sum is integrable against t by Tonelli and has strictly positive density on t>0. Differentiating the locally convergent log product yields the cumulants and strict complete monotonicity of the mean; the zeta sum and coth formula yield both endpoint limits. Symmetry exchanges or equates the target laws. No conditional completion-time moment difference is asserted when that difference is undefined. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed; its finite mixture tests are for the i.i.d. special case only.

originality.rationale: PASS for the repaired, specifically scoped full conditional-time convolution invariant under history-dependent return with fresh exploration. The no-overhead ratio follows from published conditional renewal currents and standard Dirichlet weights, and the positive infinitely divisible spectral delay law follows in substance from the classical hyperbolic laws. Neither is claimed as a new renewal formula or a new class of infinitely divisible distributions. The strongest inspected finite-return result identifies invariant splitting probabilities, not the entire independent-delay relation with arbitrary adapted, potentially dependent return durations. Related distributional factorization and return overhead works are distinguished below. The priority finding is evidence-bounded, with a significant inaccessible-source risk.
residual_risks: Bressloff's full text remained unavailable; a more general marked renewal transform covering finite-return laws could reduce the original i.i.d. contribution still further. Equivalent full-history formulations may exist under sequential trial or restart terminology.

value.rationale: The replacement identifies an exact, protocol-independent distributional difference for competing targets while permitting physically meaningful dependent and history-adaptive returns. One can change both marginal timing laws, even eliminate their finite moments, without changing the convolution factor. That is a useful invariant and a stronger test of protocol models than invariant splitting or mean differences; the explicit spectral construction makes it evaluable.
